title: Understanding the Minimum Wage Victoria 15 Year Old Rate and How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay
description: Learn how the minimum wage Victoria 15 year old rate compares to the National Minimum Wage, and use our hourly to annual conversion with casual loading and super paid on top.
salarySummary: For a 15-year-old in Victoria, the minimum wage is a percentage of the adult rate under the relevant award; the National Minimum Wage for adults is $26.44 per hour for 38 hours per week.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for a 15-year-old in Victoria?
faqs.a: The minimum wage for a 15-year-old in Victoria depends on the applicable award or enterprise agreement. Under most awards, junior employees receive a percentage of the adult rate – for example, 50% to 60% of the National Minimum Wage for a 15-year-old. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides specific award rates. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour applies to adult employees not covered by an award.

faqs.q: Does casual loading apply to the minimum wage for a 15-year-old?
faqs.a: Yes, if a 15-year-old is employed as a casual, they are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of their base hourly rate. For example, if the base junior rate is $13.22 per hour (50% of $26.44), the casual rate would be $16.53 per hour. The loading compensates for lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for a 15-year-old earning minimum wage?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). For a 15-year-old, the super guarantee applies if they earn $450 or more before tax in a calendar month. The super is calculated on the base hourly rate (including casual loading if applicable) and is paid into a super fund. It does not reduce take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting an Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

When you have an hourly rate, the standard formula to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This calculator assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For full-time employees, we use 38 hours per week, which is the ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the hours accordingly.

For example, an adult on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour working 38 hours per week earns:

- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (rounded to $1,004.9 in official figures)
- Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44
- Annual: $1,004.72 × 52 = $52,245.44

### The Minimum Wage Victoria 15 Year Old Context

If you are looking up the **minimum wage victoria 15 year old**, note that junior rates apply. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour is for adult employees (21 and over, or 20 in some awards). For a 15-year-old, the applicable award or the National Minimum Wage Order sets a percentage of the adult rate. For example, under the General Retail Industry Award, a 15-year-old receives 50% of the adult rate. That would be $13.22 per hour. Always check the specific award with the Fair Work Ombudsman.

Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details on adult and junior rates. To see how your hourly rate converts to annual pay, use [the timesheet](/) and enter your base rate.

## Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

A key feature of this calculator is the option to add 25% casual loading. Casual loading is an extra payment on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid sick leave, annual leave, or public holiday pay. The loading is applied before calculating annual pay.

For example, a casual adult on the National Minimum Wage:

- Base rate: $26.44 per hour
- Casual rate: $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour
- Annual gross (38 hours/week): $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12%. Super is calculated on your base hourly rate (including casual loading if applicable) and is paid into your super fund. It does not reduce your take-home pay. The super contribution stops once your earnings reach the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

For a 15-year-old casual on the junior minimum wage (say $13.22 per hour base):

- Casual rate: $13.22 × 1.25 = $16.53 per hour
- Annual gross (38 hours): $16.53 × 38 × 52 = $32,663.28
- Super (12% of ordinary earnings): $13.22 × 38 × 52 × 0.12 = $3,139.78 (note: super is on base, not casual loading, but check your award)

Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains the rules in more detail.

## Tax and Medicare

After calculating your annual gross pay, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. This calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. The levy may be reduced for low-income earners.

For a 15-year-old earning $32,663.28 (casual junior example):

- Tax: ($32,663.28 – $18,200) × 0.15 = $2,169.49
- Medicare: $32,663.28 × 0.02 = $653.27
- Net annual: $32,663.28 – $2,169.49 – $653.27 = $29,840.52

Remember, this is an estimate. Your actual tax may differ if you have a HELP debt, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

## Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the adult minimum wage example:

- Weekly: $1,004.72
- Fortnightly: $2,009.44

If you are a casual, your fortnightly pay may vary if your hours change. The calculator assumes consistent hours each week.

## Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

It is important to distinguish between the National Minimum Wage (set by the Fair Work Commission) and award rates. The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees are covered by an award, which often provides higher minimum rates. For a 15-year-old, the award will specify a junior percentage. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) list the rates for each industry.

Our [reference tables](/data) include the National Minimum Wage and ABS Average Weekly Earnings. The ABS reported full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. For Victoria, the figure was $2,041.10 per week. These are averages, not medians for a specific job.

## Super and Packaging

Super is a key part of your total remuneration. The 12% super guarantee is paid on top of your ordinary time earnings. If you salary sacrifice, your super may be higher, but your take-home pay lower. This calculator does not include salary packaging. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

## Summary

To convert your hourly rate to annual pay:

1. Multiply your base hourly rate by hours per week (use 38 if full-time).
2. If casual, multiply by 1.25 to include loading.
3. Multiply by 52 weeks.
4. Add 12% super on top of ordinary earnings (not on loading unless specified).
5. Estimate tax and Medicare using the 2026–27 rates.

For the **minimum wage victoria 15 year old**, remember that junior rates are a percentage of the adult rate. Always check your award or the Fair Work Ombudsman for the exact figure. Use [the timesheet](/) to enter your rate and see the annual breakdown.
